set.approach: From the main Blacktail parking area, leave the lot by its northern edge on the trail that curls around Blacktail Butte until the small north-facing cliff comes into view; a spur trail leads up to it. The route is on the right side of the wall, below the top of the cliff, and starts with a move out of the overhanging cave at its foot.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; location and anchor access from the route page. Lead review dropped the descent: it described reaching the top anchor, not getting down.

set.approach: From the parking lot, cross the sidewalk to the trail, which bears right into the trees and zigzags uphill; do not take the left branch, which climbs steps to the boulder traverse and dead-ends. The route starts a short way right of Higher Education, with a textured start into a crack or edge, and shares its anchor.

review.notes: Both pages. Route is filed on Lower Blacktail; fits. Lead review dropped the descent: it described reaching the top anchor, not getting down.

wy_lower_blacktail_butte_you_might_be_lo.skip_reason: Searched Mountain Project (search for the full name, 'might be lost', and the slug) and listed the Lower Blacktail Butte area page: no route of this name exists there or elsewhere in Wyoming. Cannot confirm the line; grade '5.10b/c X' on a top-rope row also looks mis-entered.

set.approach: From Haystack Meadows, walk the basin below the Grassy Goat Trail to Deep Lake and follow the shoreline trail around the west side; the east-side path is an alternative. The slabs on the southwest corner of the lake are climbed from a tree ledge above the water. Reese's Pass is the gentle slab beneath the exposed ledge, a short way north of Rhino's Ridge, and is climbed by lowering in to the waterline and climbing back up.

review.notes: Both pages. Descent not stated beyond lower-in style; not written.

set.approach: From Haystack Meadows, walk the basin below the Grassy Goat Trail to Deep Lake and follow the shoreline trail around the west side; the east-side path is an alternative. Rhino's Ridge is among the east-facing slabs at the southwest end of the lake, climbed from a tree ledge above the water. Lower in from the top to the waterline and climb back up, using pine trees for the anchor.

review.notes: Both pages. Descent not stated; not written.

set.approach: From Haystack Meadows, walk the basin below the Grassy Goat Trail to Deep Lake and follow the shoreline trail around the west side; the east-side path is an alternative. The slabs are climbed from a tree ledge above the water. Drop in on a rope from a pine and a cam anchor at the edge, where a large dead snag marks the top, and climb out; a large flake sits near the waterline.
